To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electrical activity evoked by a single action potential in a mechanosensory afferent in the leech is highly variable in time and space.
the action potentials of co-activated neurons, i. e. activated by the action potential of a single mechanosensory cell, do not correlate significantly.

The activity of coactivated neurons is statistically independent, i.e. the action potentials are not correlated, and this independence is due to the statistical independence of synaptic transmission.".
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the input/output relations of an isolated ganglion.
the analysis of the input/output relations and the computation in a neural network.
the analysis of the input/output relations of the nervous system, with the goal of understanding the basic computational principles of neural networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the input/output relations of the isolated leech ganglion are characterized by a high variability, a large number of activated neurons, and statistical independence among coactive neurons. .
the ganglionic network is a highly complex and dynamic system, in which the input/output relations are characterized by a high variability and statistical independence.

the leech ganglia, as a model for a distributed neural system, is a good model for neural networks in general, and that it is an excellent model for the study of the statistical properties of neuronal networks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ganglion of the medicinal leech can be used as a model for studying statistical independence of neuronal activity. . .
the leech ganglia are a very good model system to study the principles of neural computation.

we have demonstrated that a single action potential can elicit action potentials in a large population of neurons, that these action potentials show no pairwise correlation, that the population of neurons is highly heterogeneous, and that these neurons can be identified by intracellular recordings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the leech nervous system is an excellent model system to investigate the principles underlying neural computation.
the independence of the activity of coactivated neurons is a general feature of neural networks and that it can be used to improve signal-to-noise ratios in neuronal networks.
the statistical independence of neurons is a property that is often used to increase the reliability of neural processing.
